Sean / Redwood team,

Thanks for the onboarding run-through last week. Procurement asked me to get ahead of the commit drawdown mechanics so we don’t hit surprises in Q3. A few things we need to confirm: 

- How will the private-offer credits be consumed across multiple billing months if our usage drops below the committed ramp?
- What contingency options do you provide if our product usage unexpectedly falls (short-term and multi-quarter)?
- Invoice sequencing: can Redwood front-load credits to cover an early consumption spike and then reconcile later?

Tom — appreciate the context and the PDF. Short answer: yes, we support staged credit sequencing + explicit contingency unwind paths, and we can export an invoice-level timing matrix that your finance team can use to reconcile. High level proposal below: 

1) Tiered drawdown windows
   - Phase 1 (months 1–3): consumption credits applied at invoice close; shortfall covered by reserved buffer credits we temporarily front-load.
   - Phase 2 (months 4–6): buffers step down, consumption reconciled against actual usage.

2) Contingency options
   - Auto-throttle: we can set a utilization cap and route excess requests to a lower-cost model variant when the commit is in danger of being underutilized.
   - Credit bank: convert up to X% of committed credits to a holdback that can be applied against future spikes.

3) Invoice sequencing & reconciliation
   - We can front-load up to one invoice cycle worth of credits upon activation for immediate spikes, then reconcile in the subsequent two cycles with line-item adjustments.

Please see the initial working workbook attached (drawdown_plan_v1.xlsx) — it includes an example invoice timing matrix and a step-by-step ops checklist. Proposed next steps: 30-min sync with Aurora finance + your procurement rep + our billing ops to finalize numeric thresholds and the legal language for the PO.

Available windows: Thu 6/10 10:00–11:00 PT or Fri 6/11 14:00–15:00 PT. Which works?

—Sean
